function: Channel estimation: H-FNO maps noisy channel measurements at M pilot FIM shapes plus a target shape to the channel at that target shape (p. 10).
system: Base station with 8x8 FIM (flexible planar array, 64 elements) serving K=4 single-antenna users; TDD uplink pilots; 28 GHz mmWave; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 12).
method: Hierarchical Fourier neural operator (U-shaped, skip connections), supervised end-to-end MSE training on synthetic data; fine-tuning for new array sizes (pp. 10-13).
data_channel: Own synthetic clustered mmWave channel (L=5 clusters, G=6 paths, path-loss exponent 2.2, complex Gaussian gains); 20,000 training samples; 500 Monte Carlo test trials per SNR (p. 12).
test_conditions: Train: 8x8 FIM, max deformation lambda/2, L=5 clusters, SNR 0-20 dB. Test: sizes 10x10 to 14x14 (zero-shot, fine-tuned), deformation 0.25 and 1.00 lambda, L=20 clusters (pp. 12-14).
baselines: Classical: nearest-neighbor, KNN local-linear, kernel ridge regression, OMP, sparse Bayesian learning; learned: none; perfect CSI as sum-rate upper bound (pp. 5-8, 13).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR and versus pilot overhead M; sum rate with zero-forcing beamforming; robustness to hardware imperfections; interpretability visualizations (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Inference O(L d_v N log N) with L=2L_enc+1 Fourier layers; training per epoch O((N_s/B_s) L d_v N log N); no runtime or parameter count (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 4: "Following the mmWave channel modeling in 3GPP [31]"; the channel is the authors' own clustered model with power-law path loss and CN(0,1) gains, with no TR 38.901 scenario, CDL/TDL profile, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "trained on an FIM with a specific size N = 8×8, can be directly applied to FIMs of various other sizes from N = 10 × 10 to N = 14 × 14 without retraining"; p. 14: "trained on channels with L = 5 clusters, is tested on a more complex rich-scattering environment with L = 20 clusters".
q3_support: p. 13: "outperforms all other conventional model-based algorithms"; the baselines (nearest, KNN, KRR, OMP, SBL) are all presented as model-based in Section III (p. 5), and no earlier learned estimator or standard neural network is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "the total inference complexity is approximately O(L d_v N log N)" (math written in plain text), plus the training complexity per epoch.
q5_support: p. 12: "a dataset of N_s = 20, 000 samples is synthetically generated" with the authors' own simulator; no code or data link or DOI appears anywhere in the paper, including the conclusion and references (pp. 15-16).
notes: ris=0: the FIM is the base-station transmit array (radiating elements displaced perpendicular to the surface), not a reflecting RIS; reviewer may confirm. q1 is borderline: the paper says its channel follows 3GPP [31] (TR 38.901 V16.1.0, p. 16 ref. 31) only for the clustered form, with own parameters (L=5, G=6, exponent 2.2); marked 0 as a custom simulator. q3: KNN and KRR are called model-based by the paper and are fitted per sample on the pilots, so no learned baseline is counted. Pages 14-15 body text is not extractable as text; it was read from the page images.
